title: Interfaces, default methods and multiple inheritance of behaviour

videos.script: A class can extend one other class. It can implement as many interfaces as it likes. This lesson is about what an interface is, and why that difference matters. {{contract}} First, an interface as a contract. Lendable says a thing has a title and a loan period. A book and a DVD sign it, and a list of Lendables holds both. {{refuse}} The compiler holds them to it. Leave a method out and the class does not compile. {{defaults}} Then default methods: how an interface grows a new method without breaking every class that already signed it. {{diamond}} Two interfaces with the same default method meet in one class, and the compiler refuses to guess. You choose, in one line. {{sealed}} Last, a sealed interface, which names every class allowed to implement it. That list lets a switch know it has covered every case. By the end you can design a small contract and say who may sign it.
